Title: Update an existing order with status 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' and verify the changes are reflected
Section: Order Management: Update an existing order
Preconditions: An existing order with status 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' exists in the system (orderId known)
Expected Result: 1. HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing the updated order summary. 2. HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing the full order details, including updated fields: customerName='Updated Customer Name', customerPhone='5551234567', totalAmount=2500.00, paidAmount=1000.00, dueAmount=1500.00, trialDate='2024-12-20', deliveryDate='2024-12-25', and the updated measurement values.

Title: Attempt to update an existing order with status other than 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' and verify the update is rejected
Section: Order Management: Update an existing order with invalid status
Preconditions: An existing order with status other than 'MEASUREMENT_DONE' exists in the system (orderId known)
Steps:
1. Send a PUT request to /api/orders/{orderId} with the payload in testData.

Test Data: {
  "customerName": "Updated Customer Name",
  "customerPhone": "5551234567",
  "customerGender": "male",
  "orderGender": "male",
  "totalAmount": 2500.00,
  "paidAmount": 1000.00,
  "dueAmount": 1500.00,
  "trialDate": "2024-12-20",
  "deliveryDate": "2024-12-25",
  "shopId": 1,
  "items": []
}
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request response with an error message: 'Order update not allowed. Status is already <current status>'.

Title: Retrieve the last measurement details for a customer and item combination and verify the correct measurements are returned
Section: Order Management: Retrieve last measurement for a customer and item
Preconditions: An existing order with measurements for the given customer phone and item ID exists in the system
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement with query parameters phone and itemId as specified in testData.

Test Data: phone=5551234567&itemId=1
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"itemName": "<item name>", "measurements": [{"id": <non-null number>, "name": "Chest", "unit": "cm", "value": 95.0}, {"id": <non-null number>, "name": "Waist", "unit": "cm", "value": 85.0}]}

Title: Retrieve all orders for a shop filtered by order gender and verify the results are correct
Section: Order Management: Retrieve orders by shop and order gender
Preconditions: Existing orders for the given shop ID and order gender exist in the system
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/{shopId}/orderGender/{orderGender} with path variables as specified in testData.

Test Data: shopId=1&orderGender=male
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing a list of order summaries for the shop with orderGender='male'. Each order summary includes: orderId, shopName, customerName, totalAmount, paidAmount, dueAmount, orderDate, trialDate, deliveryDate, and status.

Title: Verify that order update enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot update another user's order
Preconditions: 1. Two users (User A and User B) exist in the system. 2. User A has an existing order with ID 1001 and status MEASUREMENT_DONE. 3. User B is authenticated but does not own order 1001.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and the order is not updated. No order details are returned in the response body.

Title: Verify that order update rejects attempts when order status is not MEASUREMENT_DONE
Preconditions: 1. User A has an existing order with ID 1002 and status PENDING (not MEASUREMENT_DONE). 2. User A is authenticated and owns order 1002.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and an error message indicating that the order update is not allowed due to its current status (e.g., 'Order update not allowed. Status is already PENDING').

Title: Verify that order update does not expose sensitive system details in error messages
Preconditions: 1. No order exists with ID 999999. 2. User A is authenticated.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a generic error message (e.g., 'Order not found with ID: 999999') without revealing internal system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that last measurement retrieval enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot access another user's measurements
Preconditions: 1. Two users (User A and User B) exist in the system. 2. User A has an existing order with measurements for item ID 1. 3. User B is authenticated but does not own any orders for item ID 1.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User B. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement?phone=+1234567890&itemId=1 (where +1234567890 is User A's phone number).
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and no measurement data is returned in the response body.

Title: Verify that last measurement retrieval rejects injection attempts via special characters in phone number input
Preconditions: 1. User A is authenticated. 2. No customer exists with phone number containing special characters.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User A. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement?phone=+1234567890' OR '1'='1&itemId=1.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) or 404 (Not Found), and no measurement data is returned in the response body.

Title: Verify that last measurement retrieval does not expose sensitive system details in error messages
Preconditions: 1. User A is authenticated. 2. No customer exists with phone number +9999999999. 3. No item exists with ID 999999.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User A. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement?phone=+9999999999&itemId=999999.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a generic error message (e.g., 'No last measurement found') without revealing internal system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that last measurement retrieval handles oversized phone number input to prevent overflow or denial of service
Preconditions: 1. User A is authenticated.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User A. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/last-measurement?phone=+1234567890123456789012345678901234567890&itemId=1 (phone number exceeds 30 characters).
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and an error message indicating that the phone number length exceeds the allowed limit.

Title: Verify that order retrieval by shop ID and gender enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot access another shop's orders
Section: Order Management - Order Retrieval by Shop and Gender
Preconditions: 1. Two shops (Shop A and Shop B) exist in the system. 2. User A is authenticated and belongs to Shop A. 3. Shop B has existing orders with gender MALE.
Steps: 1. Authenticate as User A. 2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/shop/2/orderGender/MALE (where 2 is Shop B's ID).
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and no order data is returned in the response body.

Title: Verify that order update rejects path traversal sequences in photo URLs to prevent unauthorized file access
Preconditions: 1. User A is authenticated and owns an existing order with ID 1003 and status MEASUREMENT_DONE.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and an error message indicating invalid photo URL (e.g., 'Invalid photo URL format').

Title: Verify that order update rejects malformed or excessively large measurement values to prevent overflow or injection
Preconditions: 1. User A is authenticated and owns an existing order with ID 1004 and status MEASUREMENT_DONE.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and an error message indicating invalid measurement value (e.g., 'Measurement value exceeds allowed limit').

Title: Verify the addition of spring-tx dependency does not break existing transactional operations or introduce conflicts
Preconditions: Application built with the updated pom.xml, all dependencies resolved, and database connection configured
Steps:
1. Deploy the application with the updated configuration. 2. Trigger an operation that involves transaction management (e.g., order creation with image uploads). 3. Observe the logs for transaction-related errors or warnings. 4. Verify the operation completes successfully without rollback or unexpected behavior.

Test Data: New dependency: org.springframework:spring-tx (version inherited from parent POM). Existing operations: order creation with image uploads (ID=d9f8e47-TC-013, ID=d9f8e47-TC-014).
Expected Result: Order creation and other transactional operations complete successfully. No transaction-related errors (e.g., 'No qualifying bean of type PlatformTransactionManager') appear in logs. Rollback behavior remains unchanged for failed operations.

Title: Verify transitive dependency conflicts do not arise from the addition of spring-tx
Preconditions: Application built with the updated pom.xml, dependency tree generated (e.g., using `mvn dependency:tree`)
Steps:
1. Generate the dependency tree for the project. 2. Check for version conflicts or duplicate dependencies related to Spring (e.g., spring-core, spring-beans, spring-tx). 3. Deploy the application. 4. Verify no ClassNotFoundException, NoSuchMethodError, or other runtime errors related to Spring dependencies appear in logs.

Test Data: New dependency: org.springframework:spring-tx. Potential conflicts: existing Spring dependencies (e.g., spring-context, spring-web).
Expected Result: Dependency tree shows no version conflicts for Spring dependencies. Application starts without runtime errors related to Spring or transaction management.

Title: Verify the project builds successfully with the new dependency and produces the correct artifact
Preconditions: Clean local Maven repository or use `mvn clean install`
Steps:
1. Run `mvn clean install` on the project. 2. Verify the build completes without errors. 3. Check the target directory for the generated artifact (e.g., JAR/WAR file). 4. Verify the artifact size and contents are consistent with expectations (no unexpected dependencies or missing classes).

Test Data: New dependency: org.springframework:spring-tx. Build command: `mvn clean install`.
Expected Result: Build completes with SUCCESS status. Artifact is generated in the target directory with no missing or unexpected dependencies. No build errors related to dependency resolution.
